body.title: Floor access depends on an endorsement that works like a queue
body.body:

body.title: Common floor belongs to every member; membership needs no approval
body.body:
## What changed (index.html, the component source)
- **Economy paragraph:** "the basic capacity floor of approved members" becomes "of every member".
- **NOT A MERIT PRIZE card:** "The floor is for approved members, and approval has requirements of integration and collaboration." becomes "The floor belongs to every member; while resources are scarce, access goes through a queue weighted by context, not through an approval."
- **Distributed Support glossary entry:** "ensuring approved members baseline access…" becomes "ensuring every member baseline access…"; "Approval has requirements of integration and collaboration." becomes "While the network cannot sustain it for everyone, access goes through a queue weighted by context, such as need and urgency, and the floor grows with abundance."
- **Mirrored contracts:** Distributed Support scope and Value Unit non-scope lines follow their repositories (draykerdk/distributed-support, draykerdk/value-unit PRs on the same branch name).

## Why
Being a member requires no approval: anyone becomes a member by being a person and creating their UID. The common floor belongs to every member; under scarcity it is a context-weighted queue, never an approval and never a function of reputation.

## Checks
`node --check support.js`, `node --check drayker-mark.js`, `node tools/render-check.js`, `node tools/prerender-check.js --site=org` and `git diff --check` pass. The drayker.com mirror is regenerated in draykerdk/drayker.com on the same branch name.

body.title: Merge the organization snapshot directly once its check passes
body.body:
## Diagnosis

- The daily run pushes `automation/org-snapshot`, reuses or opens the PR, enables `gh pr merge --auto` and dispatches `drayker-component.yml` on the branch.
- PR #18 (opened 2026-09-25) kept auto-merge enabled and was force-pushed every day until 2026-10-06. The dispatched `component-contract / Validate public evidence contract` check passed on each head commit, and the ruleset needs no approvals, but the PR never merged.
- The only snapshot PR that auto-merged (#16) did so seconds after a maintainer pushed to it, which started an ordinary `pull_request` run. A check run started by the workflow token does not wake auto-merge.

## Fix

After dispatching the check, the workflow waits for that run on the exact head commit (`gh run watch --exit-status`), merges with `gh pr merge --squash --match-head-commit`, and deletes the branch. A failed check or a refused merge now fails the run instead of leaving a silent open PR. The ruleset is untouched and nothing is pushed to master directly.

  • PR #18 (opened 2026-09-25) kept auto-merge enabled and was force-pushed every day until 2026-10-06. The dispatched component-contract / Validate public evidence contract check passed on each head commit, and the ruleset needs no approvals, but the PR never merged.
  • The only snapshot PR that auto-merged (#16) did so seconds after a maintainer pushed to it, which started an ordinary pull_request run. A check run started by the workflow token does not wake auto-merge.

Fix

After dispatching the check, the workflow waits for that run on the exact head commit (gh run watch --exit-status), merges with gh pr merge --squash --match-head-commit, and deletes the branch. body.title: Name the real snapshot blocker and restore auto-merge
body.body:
## Corrected diagnosis

#42 assumed that auto-merge simply was not woken by a check started with the workflow token. A test run after #42 (run 37593342985, PR #43) showed otherwise. The direct `gh pr merge` was refused by the base branch policy while the dispatched check had passed.

- The PR status rollup had no checks at all. A `workflow_dispatch` run on the branch does not satisfy the required `component-contract / Validate public evidence contract` check on a pull request.
- The run that counts is the `pull_request` run on the PR head. GitHub holds it as `action_required`, because the repository approval policy is `first_time_contributors` and the PR author, github-actions[bot], counts as one. This happened every day since 2026-09-25.
- Once a maintainer approved that run, it passed and the PR went from BLOCKED to CLEAN (PR #43, merged after checking that `data/org.json` carries the current repository descriptions).

## Change

- Restores `gh pr merge --squash --auto` and removes the wait and direct merge from #42, which can only fail.
- Removes the dispatch, which does not count for the required check.
- Prints a run notice naming the PR whose run needs approval.
- Corrects the comment in `drayker-component.yml`.

Making the snapshot fully automatic needs a maintainer decision: approve the run each day, change the Actions approval policy, or push with a token that is not github-actions[bot].

body.title: fix: organization snapshot reads open issues through search
body.body:
The scheduled **Organization snapshot** has failed every day since 2026-08-13 with `refusing empty issue snapshot`. The workflow token is scoped to this repository, so `repos/<r>/issues` returned empty lists for the other repositories. The guard did its job: it refused to publish an empty board.

This PR builds the issue list from the search API, which reads public data with any token. Pull requests are still dropped explicitly by the `pull_request` key, and only non-archived component repositories are kept. It also grants `issues: read`.

Verified locally with the same script: 25 repositories, 24 issues, 2 contributors, the same 24 issues as the per-repository method.

body.title: Open the mother pages with the argument, not with the machinery
body.body:
Five portal pages led with system vocabulary before giving a stranger a reason to care:

| Page | Opened with |
|---|---|
| Dk | "intelligence, organization and computing as one distributed architecture" |
| Ecosystem | "Each part below is meant to be public, replaceable and owned by nobody" |
| Organization | "Drayker is in its founding phase" |
| Partnerships | "a protocol for distributed collaboration" |
| Volunteer | "a unified system of intelligence, organization and computing" |

Each is accurate, and each answers a question nobody has asked yet. Every one now opens with one sentence anyone can read, tying the page to the thesis the rest of the site tells, before any term from the system appears.

The rest of the copy is untouched. Reading the pages, they were not written in an old voice — they were missing their first line. Volunteer keeps "volunteer, non-profit" inside the sentence rather than only in the badge below it, since that one sets expectations.

**Verified:** 113,559 static checks, 833 prerender checks across 39 routes, and the pages read in the browser.

`drayker.com` is generated from this component; its regeneration is in [drayker.com#…] and should merge after this one.

body.title: Write the first-time contributor guide
body.body:
## What is delivered
A guide for someone who has just decided to contribute and does not know the system: where the map is, how a function is claimed, how pull requests to `master` are checked and discussed, and what happens after they open their first pull request.

## Why it is needed
The portal explains that you do not need to know the whole system to contribute to it. It does not yet explain the first twenty minutes.

## Where to start
The DFM page and the open-functions board describe the shape of the work. This function is the missing bridge between "I want to help" and the first claimed function.

Where it lives is part of the function — this repository, or `dknowledge` alongside CONTRIBUTING.md.

---
This is an open function: small enough for one person to finish, defined enough that the result composes with the rest. Claim it in this thread before starting so two people do not carry the same function, and deliver through a pull request to `master`. It appears on the board at https://drayker.org/#org/fn
